# Results — Study 143 (Dividend-Capture) on real unadjusted daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The dividend-capture
strategy: buy at the close on the trading day before the ex-dividend date (t-1), collect
the dividend on the ex-date (t), sell at the close the day after (t+1). Tested across a
basket of 8 US stocks and ETFs with long dividend histories using **unadjusted** daily
prices (auto-adjust=False from yfinance), because backward-adjusted prices distribute the
dividend adjustment across all historical bars and do not show the raw ex-date price
mechanics. As-of **2026-06-14**, events 2000-01-06 to 2026-05-26; total n = 823 events
(8 tickers × ~103 quarterly dividends). Spin-off events removed (div > 5% of price): 2 events
excluded, clean sample n = 821.*

## The ex-date price drop vs the dividend

The efficient-markets null predicts that on the ex-dividend date, the unadjusted stock price
drops by exactly the dividend amount, so the ratio ``drop / dividend = 1.0``. Capture is
only profitable if this ratio is *systematically below 1*.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| n events (clean) | 821 |
| Mean drop/div | **+1.11** |
| Median drop/div | +1.04 |
| Std drop/div | 2.11 |
| Fraction drop < div (gross profit) | **48.7%** |
| HAC *t* vs H0: ratio = 1.0 | **+1.45** |
| Mean drop (bps of price) | +93.8 bps |
| Mean div  (bps of price) | +82.8 bps |

The drop ratio is **+1.11 on average**: the market takes back slightly *more* than the full
dividend in price. The HAC t-stat vs 1.0 is **+1.45** — not statistically significant, and
in the *wrong* direction for the capture hypothesis. Only 48.7% of events have a drop smaller
than the dividend; a coin flip. No evidence of systematic under-adjustment.

## The capture trade P&L

Buy at close t-1, sell at close t+1, collect the dividend. Round-trip cost = 5 bps.

| Arm | n | Win-rate | Mean (bps/trade) | Skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Capture (gross, no cost)** | 821 | 46.3% | **−12.9** | +0.25 | **−1.85** |
| Capture (net, 5 bps RT) | 821 | 46.3% | **−17.9** | +0.25 | **−2.59** |
| Capture (net, 10 bps RT) | 821 | 46.3% | −22.9 | +0.25 | −3.34 |

- Gross mean is **−12.9 bps/trade**, HAC *t* = **−1.85** — negative and near the significance
  threshold, consistent with the market taking back slightly more than the dividend in price.
- At 5 bps round-trip cost (conservative for electronic equities), net mean = **−17.9 bps**,
  HAC *t* = **−2.59** (statistically significant at the 5% level — a *significant loser*).
- At ~31 ex-date events per year per ticker (8 tickers = ~248 trades/yr), costs compound
  severely: at 5 bps, the annual drag from costs alone is ~8 bps × 248 = ~20% of capital if
  fully concentrated — though realistic sizing would be far smaller.

No ticker shows a statistically significant positive gross capture return (|*t*| < 2 everywhere,
and 6 of 8 have negative point estimates). VYM, JNJ, and KO show positive gross returns but
with |*t*| < 1.1 — indistinguishable from noise.

## Cost sweep

| Round-trip cost | Net (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −12.9 | −1.85 |
| 5.0 bps | −17.9 | −2.59 |
| 10.0 bps | −22.9 | −3.34 |
| 20.0 bps | −32.9 | −4.82 |
| 50.0 bps | −62.9 | −9.28 |

Since the gross return is already negative, there is **no positive break-even cost**: every
basis point of cost widens the loss. At 5 bps (realistic for a retail electronic broker), the
trade is a statistically certified loser.

## Synthetic positive control

On the deterministic synthetic tape (``data.synthetic_events``), the strategy correctly
recovers a gross profit when we plant partial market inefficiency (``efficiency > 0``):

| Planted efficiency (fraction div not recouped in price) | Mean drop/div | Gross (bps) | Profitable? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (fully efficient / EMH null) | ~1.00 | ~+13 | no (|t| < 2) |
| 0.25 (price drops by 75% of div)  | ~0.75 | ~+38 | yes |
| 0.50 (price drops by 50% of div)  | ~0.50 | ~+63 | yes |
| 1.00 (no price adjustment at all) | ~0.00 | ~+113| yes |

The machinery works correctly: the real-tape result of −12.9 bps is consistent with an
efficiency very close to 0 (fully efficient market) — if anything slightly *over*-efficient
(price drops slightly more than the dividend).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Gross mean = −12.9 bps/trade, HAC *t* = −1.85 (negative, near threshold);
  drop/div = 1.11, HAC *t* vs 1.0 = +1.45 (no under-adjustment). No statistically real
  evidence that the market systematically under-prices the ex-dividend drop. If anything, the
  market slightly *over*-adjusts.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross is already negative; at 5 bps cost net *t* = −2.59 (a
  statistically certified loser). No positive break-even cost exists.
- **Capture premium? — None.** Efficient markets (and the tax framework for institutional
  holders) ensure the ex-date drop fully reflects the dividend. The "free" dividend is not
  free: you pay for it in the price.
